VBO:0200872.summary: Loyal to its handler and sometimes reserved at first meetings, the McNab Shepherd is described by its foundation as eager to work. Its herding style is upright and loose-eyed: it goes to the head of livestock to gather and hold them. A keen nose helps locate stock hidden in brush.
VBO:0200872.shortDescription: A loyal working stockdog, gathering livestock with an upright, loose-eyed style and finding hidden animals by scent.

sources.title: McNab Stockdog Foundation — Broad working breed standard SGSTD2101.000
sources.evidence: Loyal handler bond and initial reserve; upright loose-eyed gathering/head-and-hold style, keen nose finding stock in brush. Medium lean slightly longer-than-tall body,14–26in/30–60lb range, moderate head/muzzle/oval eyes, erect or semi-erect ears; long tails most common, bob/dock forms occur but not selected. Short-to-medium flat bi/tri-color coat, balanced normal functional limbs/paws.

VBO:0201394.summary: Friendly and open, though sometimes reserved on first meeting, the Waller is described by its breed association as an intelligent dog that enjoys work. The association gives it a broad role spanning family life, sport and herding. Its standard favors quick, flexible movement rather than a heavy build.
VBO:0201394.shortDescription: A friendly, work-loving dog whose association describes family, sport and herding roles, with some initial reserve.

sources.title: Wäller Freunde Zuchtgemeinschaft im IHR — Wäller standard
sources.evidence: Friendly open dog sometimes reserved at first meeting, intelligent willing to work; named family/sport/herding role. Square medium55cm±5female/60±5male medium bone, long straight/wavy coat>=7cm moderate undercoat/beard/brows, high-set drop/tip ears, full low furnished tail to hock with light open end hook, four normal muscular limbs/compact paws. Caption explicitly names Cara-Mia von den Wolkentauchern.

VBO:0201433.summary: Happy, athletic and energetic in breeder Roz Wardrop’s account, the Working Cocker Spaniel brings a strong hunting drive to its handler’s work. Working lines are selected for intelligence, speed and hunting style rather than coat colour. Finding and flushing game is their central job, from rabbits to pheasants.
VBO:0201433.shortDescription: A happy, energetic working Cocker, selected for hunting style and speed and bred to find and flush game.

sources.title: Cocker Spaniel Club of Scotland — Roz Wardrop on working Cockers
sources.evidence: Happy athletic energetic working Cockers bred for intelligence/speed/hunting style; finding/flushing rabbits or pheasants. Same Cocker breed as show lines, often longer/taller with higher ear set and less feathering; color secondary to work. Actual two solid working dogs pictured, no claim either is named Star.

VBO:0200352.summary: Calm and independent in Continental Kennel Club’s description, the Miniature Shar-Pei is devoted to familiar people but may stay aloof with strangers. The registry places companionship at the center of its role. It also describes a watchful dog that tends to save its bark for something that catches its attention.
VBO:0200352.shortDescription: A calm, independent miniature Shar-Pei, described as devoted to family, reserved with strangers and watchful.

sources.title: Continental Kennel Club USA — Miniature Shar-Pei standard
sources.evidence: Explicit Miniature0–17in/25–40lb, aliases Mini-Pei/Toy Shar-Pei no independent toy count. Calm independent loyal character, reserve toward strangers, companion and sentry voice. Athletic square body, moderate broad head/real deep wide muzzle, small forward-fold triangle ears, adult skin wrinkles never obscuring outline, moderate dewlap. Full high-set tapering natural tail may curve or curl to side; choose loose open curve not tight knot. Short horse coat/solid fawn black pigment and four normal compact paws.
